label: Truthful selective disclosure can conceal whether an event occurred
paraphrase: Among truthful event lists for a supplied history profile, covering all occurrences is equivalent to correctness of inferring absence from nonmembership and absence implying nonmembership. In two finite histories, a single policy reports just the later event truthfully in both, while the earlier event occurs in only one. No classifier of those disclosed lists recovers earlier occurrence across the pair. The complete lists identify that target across the pair.
